exercises.exerciseName: medicine ball reverse wood chop squat

instructions.originalText: Hold a medicine ball overhead to one side and stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down while chopping the ball diagonally across your body.
Rotate your torso and bring the ball toward the opposite knee.
Stand up as you return the ball overhead.
Alternate sides each set.
Stand on both feet with your knees slightly bent.
Swing your arms and hop forward a short distance.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Reset your posture and hop again.
Keep your hops controlled and your chest tall.
Stand sideways to a wall holding a medicine ball at your hip.
Rotate away from the wall and load your back hip.
Explosively rotate and throw the ball into the wall.
Catch it on the rebound and repeat.
Switch sides after the planned reps.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level.
Bend your knees slightly and dip your body down, then explosively extend your legs and press the dumbbells overhead.
Lock out your arms at the top of the movement, then lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: medicine ball close grip push up

instructions.originalText: Start in a high plank position with your hands on the medicine ball, shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand on one leg with a soft knee.
Hinge at the hips and reach down toward your foot or the floor.
Keep your back flat and your free leg extended behind you.
Return to standing by squeezing your glute.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
Stand on one leg with a soft knee.
Hinge forward at the hips and reach across your body.
Rotate your torso slightly as you reach.
Return to standing with control.
Complete the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.exerciseName: medicine ball single leg wood chop

instructions.originalText: Stand on one leg holding a medicine ball overhead to one side.
Chop the ball diagonally down across your body.
Rotate your torso and pivot your standing foot.
Return the ball overhead with control.
Complete the reps, then switch legs.
Place the bosu ball on the ground with the flat side up.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position yourself on top of the bosu ball.
Lower your body down by bending your knees and hips, as if sitting back into a chair.
Keep your chest up and your weight on your heels.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Kneel behind a stability ball and place your forearms on it.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Keep your neck neutral and your hips from sagging or rising.
Hold for 20-40 seconds, then lower to the floor.
Start by lying face down on a stability ball with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes touching the ground.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, keeping your back straight.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing your shoulder towards your hip. Keep your hips and legs stable throughout the movement.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie on your back with your legs extended.
Bend one knee and place your foot flat on the ground.
Using your hands or a towel, gently pull your toes towards your body, feeling a stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat on the other leg.
Lie on your back with your legs extended.
Bend your right knee and place your right ankle on your left thigh, just above the knee.
Grasp your left thigh with both hands and gently pull it towards your chest.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release and repeat on the other side.

exercises.exerciseName: assisted lying gluteus and piriformis stretch

instructions.originalText: Lie on your back with your legs extended.
Bend your right knee and place your right ankle on your left thigh, just above the knee.
Grasp your left thigh with both hands and gently pull it towards your chest.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and repeat on the other side.

exercises.exerciseName: assisted oblique glute minimus and medius stretch

instructions.originalText: Lie on your back or side while your partner supports your top leg.
Have your partner gently guide the leg across your body while you stay relaxed.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked on top of each other.
Bend your bottom leg slightly for stability.
Place your top foot on a stable surface, such as a bench or step.
Keeping your top leg straight, slowly lower it towards the ground, feeling a stretch in your inner thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
Lie face down on the ground with your legs extended.
Bend your left knee and reach back with your left hand to grab your left foot or ankle.
Gently pull your left foot towards your glutes, feeling a stretch in your left quad.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat with your right leg.
Lie face down on the ground with your legs straight.
Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grab your right foot or ankle.
Gently pull your right foot or ankle towards your glutes, feeling a stretch in the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release and repeat on the other side.

exercises.exerciseName: assisted oblique and latissimus dorsi stretch on stability ball

instructions.originalText: Lie sideways over a stability ball with your hips supported and one arm reaching overhead.
Let your partner gently guide your reaching arm further while you roll slightly over the ball.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: assisted seated pectoralis major stretch with stability ball

instructions.originalText: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a stability ball with both hands and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Slowly lower the stability ball towards your chest, feeling a stretch in your pectoral muscles.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Attach a rope to a cable machine at waist height.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip, with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull the rope towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your elbows close to your body and continue pulling until your hands reach your chest.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the rope and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: barbell seated close grip behind neck triceps extension

instructions.originalText: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the barbell with a close grip behind your neck, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your head and slowly lower the barbell towards the back of your head.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: barbell incline close grip bench press

instructions.originalText: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: barbell lying back of the head tricep extension

instructions.originalText: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.
Hold the barbell with a reverse grip, palms facing towards your face, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping your elbows in and your wrists straight.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: cable high pulley overhead tricep extension

instructions.originalText: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing away from the machine.
Grasp the rope with both hands and extend your arms overhead.
Keep your elbows close to your head and your upper arms stationary.
Slowly lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment at chest height.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and step back to create tension in the cable.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Start with your arm fully extended and perpendicular to the floor.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and push the bar down until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: cable rope high pulley overhead tricep extension

instructions.originalText: Attach a rope to a high pulley and adjust the weight accordingly.
Stand facing away from the pulley machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope with both hands, palms facing down, and bring your hands above your head.
Keep your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor.
Slowly lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Attach a rope to a high pulley and adjust the incline bench to a comfortable angle.
Stand facing away from the pulley with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight overhead.
Keep your elbows close to your head and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows until your forearms touch your biceps.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: cable rope lying on floor tricep extension

instructions.originalText: Attach a rope to a cable machine and set it to the lowest position.
Lie on the floor facing up, with your head towards the cable machine.
Hold the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and extend your arms straight up towards the ceiling.
Keep your upper arms stationary and slowly lower the rope towards your forehead, bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: cable standing reverse grip one arm overhead tricep extension

instructions.originalText: Stand facing away from the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip and extend your arm overhead, keeping your elbow close to your head.
Keep your upper arm stationary and slowly lower the cable handle behind your head by bending your elbow.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the cable handle in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, extend your forearms backwards until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower one dumbbell down towards your head, bending at the elbow, while keeping the other arm extended.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell seated bent over alternate kickback

instructions.originalText: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and parallel to the ground.
Extend one arm straight back, keeping it close to your body, until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.
Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells to your side until they are about level with your chest.
As you exhale, use your triceps to lift the dumbbells back to the starting position. Make sure to use only your triceps and do not use your forearms or biceps to help lift the dumbbells.
After a second pause at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Take a step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position.
Keep your back straight and your chest up.
Extend your arms straight overhead, keeping your elbows close to your ears.
Lower the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then straighten your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Slowly lie back on the bench, keeping the dumbbells close to your chest.
Once you are fully lying down, extend your arms straight up towards the ceiling, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your arm fully extended above your chest.
Lower the dumbbell in a controlled manner towards your forehead, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell one arm french press on exercise ball

instructions.originalText: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your arm straight up towards the ceiling, keeping your elbow stationary.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell seated bent over triceps extension

instructions.originalText: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your head up.
Extend your arms straight back, keeping your elbows close to your head.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell seated reverse grip one arm overhead tricep extension

instructions.originalText: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell with an underhand grip and extend your arm straight up overhead.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arm back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Extend your arms straight back, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides with each repetition.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell standing bent over one arm triceps extension

instructions.originalText: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and parallel to the ground.
Extend your arm straight back, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell standing bent over two arm triceps extension

instructions.originalText: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Extend your arms straight back, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: dumbbell tricep kickback with stork stance

instructions.originalText: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Bring your right elbow up to your side, keeping it bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing away from you.
Extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells down towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
As you lower the dumbbells, twist your wrists so that your palms face towards you at the bottom of the movement.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then reverse the movement by pressing the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
As you press the dumbbells up, twist your wrists back to the starting position with palms facing away from you.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place your hands on the ball beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Engage your triceps and push through your hands to lift your body off the ball, straightening your arms.
Lower your body back down by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and extend your arm straight up above your head.
Bend your elbow and lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arm close to your ear.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm.
Sit on a stability ball with a dumbbell in each hand, then walk forward until your upper back rests on the ball.
Lift your hips level and press the dumbbells straight up, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms to press them back up.
Keep your hips up for the whole set.

exercises.exerciseName: ez bar french press on exercise ball

instructions.originalText: Sit on an exercise ball and hold an EZ barbell with an overhand grip.
Extend your arms straight up, keeping your elbows close to your head.
Slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: ez bar lying close grip triceps extension behind head

instructions.originalText: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.
Hold the ez barbell with a close grip, palms facing up, and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip.
Raise the barbell above your head, fully extending your arms.
Keeping your upper arms close to your head, slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie flat on your back on a bench with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the medicine ball with both hands, extending your arms straight up above your chest.
Lower the medicine ball towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Explosively push the medicine ball upwards, extending your arms fully and throwing the ball as high as possible.
Catch the medicine ball and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Set up a barbell on a power rack at chest height.
Stand facing the barbell and position yourself underneath it, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest, with your arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell down towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in close to your body.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Adjust the seat of the smith machine so that the bar is at shoulder height.
Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully, lifting the bar off the rack and holding it directly above your chest.
Lower the bar slowly towards your forehead, keeping your elbows close to your head.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the bar back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on a bench with your hands gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your butt off the bench, supporting your weight with your hands.
Bend your elbows and lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your feet forward, sliding your butt off the bench and supporting your weight with your arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping your back close to the bench.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.
Slide your butt off the front of the bench with your legs extended in front of you.
Keep your back close to the bench and your elbows slightly bent.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Shift your weight onto your left foot and lift your right foot slightly off the ground.
Hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your right leg extended behind you for balance.
Lower the barbell towards the ground, keeping it close to your body and your left leg slightly bent.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your torso back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot slightly off the ground.
Keeping your back straight, hinge forward at the hips and lower the dumbbell towards the ground.
At the same time, extend your right leg straight behind you, maintaining a slight bend in your left knee.
Lower the dumbbell until your torso and right leg are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then engage your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Sit on the edge of a bench or have someone hold your feet down.
Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended in front of you.
Lift your right foot off the ground and extend it forward.
Slowly lower your body down by bending your left knee and pushing your hips back.
Keep your chest up and your back straight as you lower yourself down.
Lower until your left thigh is parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down into a squat position by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and lift your knees towards your chest, twisting your torso to the side as you do so.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, twisting your torso in the opposite direction.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand next to a sturdy support and hold it with one or both hands.
Lift one leg out in front of you and balance on the other.
Sit your hips back and bend your knee, lowering as far as you can control.
Keep your heel down and your knee tracking over your toes.
Press through your foot to stand, using the support only as needed, then switch legs.
Grab the pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip, palms facing away from you.
Hang freely with your arms fully extended.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and lift your legs up by flexing your hips and knees until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Let the dumbbells hang in front of your thighs, with your arms fully extended and your palms facing your body.
Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, exhale and lift the dumbbells straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Continue lifting until the dumbbells are at shoulder height, with your elbows pointing out to the sides.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie face down on a leg curl machine with your legs extended and your ankles hooked under the padded lever.
Place your hands on the side handles of the machine for support.
Keeping your upper body stationary, exhale and curl your legs upward as far as possible.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.exerciseName: weighted triceps dip on high parallel bars

instructions.originalText: Position yourself between two parallel bars with your hands gripping the bars and your arms fully extended.
Bend your elbows and lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Lie on your side with your legs extended and your head supported by your arm.
Hold your upper arm against your side and bend your elbow to curl your forearm towards your shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit on the edge of a bench with your feet wide.
Brace one elbow against the inside of the same thigh and grip the opposite leg just above the ankle.
Curl your hand toward your shoulder, lifting that leg while it pushes down to resist.
Lower the leg slowly to the floor.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.
Kneel down on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Place your hands on the ground in front of you, shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Extend your legs straight behind you, balancing on your toes and hands, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your upper body towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Start by lying face down on the ground with your legs extended and your hands placed directly under your shoulders.
Engage your core and press through your palms to lift your upper body off the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Pause at the top for a moment, squeezing your upper back muscles.
Slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a towel with one hand.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Extend your arm fully, allowing the towel to hang in front of you.
Pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the towel back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
Lie on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other.
Prop yourself up on your forearm, keeping your elbow directly below your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your head to your feet.
While keeping your core engaged, lift your top leg as high as possible without rotating your hips.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower your leg back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Start by lying on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other.
Prop yourself up on your forearm, keeping your elbow directly below your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your head to your feet.
While maintaining the side plank position, lift your top leg towards the ceiling, keeping it straight.
Slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.exerciseName: lying single straight leg hip extension

instructions.originalText: Lie face down with your legs straight and your forehead on your hands.
Tighten your abs and glutes.
Raise one straight leg a few inches off the floor.
Pause briefly at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower under control and repeat, then switch legs.
Stand tall and interlace your fingers, then raise your arms overhead.
Press your arms slightly back and lift your chest without arching your lower back.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall with your arms out to the sides and your hands at shoulder height or slightly lower.
Have your partner hold your wrists and slowly pull your arms back until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit upright on a bench or chair with your hands behind your head or arms out wide.
Have your partner stand behind you and gently draw your elbows or wrists back.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand beside a wall or doorframe and place your forearm on it with your elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Step forward and turn your body away until you feel the stretch across your chest.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand facing a wall corner and place a forearm on each wall at about shoulder height.
Step one foot forward and lean your chest into the corner until you feel a stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back with straight arms.
Lift your hands up and away from your body while opening your chest.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: standing chest stretch (with training wall bars)

instructions.originalText: Stand beside wall bars and grip a bar at about shoulder height with one hand.
Slowly turn your body away from the bars until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand or sit tall with your arms extended behind you at hip to shoulder height.
Have your partner hold your wrists and gently pull your arms back and slightly up.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Kneel in front of a bench or chair and rest your forearms or hands on it.
Sit your hips back and let your chest drop toward the floor until you feel the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit or stand with your hands clasped behind your head and your elbows wide.
Have your partner pull your elbows back as you gently tilt your trunk forward.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and reach both straight arms behind you.
Lift your arms slightly and open your chest without leaning back.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall and raise both straight arms overhead with your palms facing forward.
Reach up and slightly back, keeping your ribs down and your core lightly braced.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Lie on your back with your arms stretched out straight to the sides or overhead.
Have your partner gently press your wrists or arms down toward the floor.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: assisted pulling arms in prone position chest stretch

instructions.originalText: Lie face down with your arms out to the sides and your forehead resting on the floor.
Have your partner hold your wrists and slowly lift your arms up and back.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit or stand tall and hold the edge of the seat or a hand behind your back to anchor one shoulder down.
Tilt your head toward the opposite shoulder until you feel a stretch along your neck.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall and bring one arm across your chest at shoulder height.
Hook it with your other forearm and pull it gently closer to your chest.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall and bring one straight arm across your chest.
Use your other hand to hold it just above the elbow and draw it closer to you.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand or sit and clasp your hands or hold a support in front of you at chest height.
Round your upper back and push your hands forward while dropping your head between your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and reach both arms forward at chest height.
Round your upper back and spread your shoulder blades apart as you reach farther.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: standing reach up back rotation stretch

instructions.originalText: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and reach one arm overhead.
Rotate your upper body gently away from the raised arm and reach up and over.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall and reach both arms overhead with your palms facing each other.
Reach up and lean slightly back, keeping your lower back relaxed and your ribs down.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Lie on your back with your arms overhead and your legs straight.
Reach your fingertips up and your toes down, as if you want to get taller.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: two handed hang back stretch (with training wall bars)

instructions.originalText: Grip a wall bar overhead with both hands and walk your feet out slightly.
Let your body hang and sink your hips back, relaxing your upper back and shoulders.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Hold the cable attachment or handles with both hands at about chest height.
Lean back with straight arms and sit your hips back until you feel your back lengthen.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall and hold a pole or frame with one hand above head height.
Lean away from the arm and sit your hips slightly back to feel a stretch along your side.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and raise one arm overhead.
Lean to the opposite side from the raised arm, reaching over without twisting.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit on the floor or a bench with your knees slightly bent and your feet flat.
Round your back and fold your chest toward your thighs, letting your arms hang down.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: seated lower trunk extensor lateral flexor stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit tall on a chair or bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Fold forward and reach your hands toward one foot, letting your trunk bend slightly to that side.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat and your knees apart.
Bend forward from your hips and let your head and arms hang between your knees.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit tall with your legs crossed or your feet flat and place one hand on the floor beside you.
Reach your other arm up and over your head toward the side, lengthening along your flank.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: sitting cross legged reach forward stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit on the floor with your legs crossed and your back tall.
Walk your hands forward along the floor and fold from your hips until you feel a stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat.
Draw both knees toward your chest and hold them with your hands.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: sitting feet together reach forward stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet together and your knees falling out.
Hold your feet and fold forward from your hips, keeping your spine long.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Pull one knee toward your chest with both hands while the other leg stays flat.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand tall, using a wall for balance if needed.
Lift one knee and pull it gently toward your chest with both hands.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders.
Place one hand behind your head and rotate your elbow up toward the ceiling.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at chest height.
Rotate your upper body to one side, keeping your hips facing forward.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Extend one arm in front of you with your palm facing up.
Use your other hand to gently press the fingers down and back until you feel the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Extend one arm in front of you with your elbow straight and palm down.
Use your other hand to rotate the palm outward until you feel a stretch along your forearm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: extension of arms in vertical stretch

instructions.originalText: Stand tall with your arms raised straight overhead.
Press your arms back slightly and reach long through your fingertips.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Place your hands or forearms on a bench or other stable support behind you.
Lower your body slightly and lean away until you feel a stretch in the front of your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Grip a pull-up bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Let your body hang with your arms straight, relaxing your shoulders downward.
Take as much weight through your legs as you need to stay comfortable.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: suspension in pulley machine in supination stretch

instructions.originalText: Hold a pulley handle with an underhand grip and your arm straight.
Lean your body weight back gently until you feel a stretch in the biceps and forearm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit at a preacher bench and rest your upper arms on the pad, holding an EZ bar.
Let the bar lower under control until your arms are fully extended, using a light load.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: elbow extension and supination pronation forearm stretch

instructions.originalText: Extend one arm in front of you with your elbow straight.
Slowly rotate your palm up and down and let your other hand add gentle pressure at each end.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.

exercises.exerciseName: wrist ulnar deviator and extensor stretch

instructions.originalText: Extend one arm in front of you with the palm down.
Bend the wrist so your fingers point down.
Gently tilt the hand toward the little finger side.
Use the other hand to apply light pressure.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: wrist radial deviator and extensor stretch

instructions.originalText: Extend one arm in front of you with the palm down.
Bend the wrist so your fingers point down.
Gently tilt the hand toward the thumb side.
Use the other hand to apply light pressure.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: wrist radial deviator and flexor stretch

instructions.originalText: Extend one arm in front of you with the palm up.
Use your other hand to pull the fingers back toward you.
Gently tilt the hand toward the thumb side.
Keep the elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch arms.

exercises.exerciseName: wrist ulnar deviator and flexor stretch

instructions.originalText: Extend one arm in front of you with the palm up.
Use your other hand to pull the fingers back toward you.
Gently tilt the hand toward the little finger side.
Keep the elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch arms.
Extend one arm forward with your palm facing up or out.
Use your other hand to gently pull your fingers and palm back toward you.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Extend one arm forward with your palm facing down and your wrist relaxed.
Use your other hand to gently press your fingers and hand down toward you.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Raise one arm overhead, bend the elbow and drop your hand behind your head.
Use your other hand to press your elbow gently back and down.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Stand next to a wall and place your bent elbow on it above head height.
Lean your body forward and down until you feel the stretch along the back of your upper arm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Extend one arm forward and bend the elbow fully with your palm down.
Use your other hand to press your forearm toward your upper arm, then rotate it gently.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly turn your head to one side, then to the other, as far as is comfortable.
Keep your chin level and avoid pushing into any pain.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit tall and gently turn your head about 45 degrees to one side.
Drop your chin diagonally toward your chest, using your hand for light added pressure.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly tilt your head back to look up at the ceiling, keeping your jaw relaxed.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breathing slow and steady.
Hold for 20-30 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one-sided.
Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Keep your eyes level and slide your chin and head straight forward.
Stop when you feel a stretch at the back of the neck.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Draw your head back to neutral and relax.
Sit tall on a chair with your hands resting in your lap.
Slowly lower your chin toward your chest.
Let the weight of your head do the work, without forcing it.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Lift your head back to neutral slowly.
Stand or sit tall with your shoulders down.
Place both hands lightly behind your head.
Let your elbows drop forward and ease your head toward your chest.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Release your hands and return to neutral.
Sit tall with your back straight.
Tuck your chin toward your chest.
Rest one hand on the back of your head and add very light pressure down.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Remove your hand and lift your head slowly.
Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Turn your head about 45 degrees to one side.
Rest a hand on the back of your head and ease your nose toward your armpit.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Lift your chin and slowly tilt your head back.
Keep the movement small and comfortable.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Return your head to neutral.
Sit or stand tall with your shoulders down.
Turn your head slightly to one side.
Tilt your chin up and back until you feel a stretch along the front of your neck.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Clasp your hands behind your head.
Gently lift your head and ease your chin toward your chest.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Lower your head back down slowly.
Lie on your back with your head near the edge of a bench or bed, shoulders supported.
Slowly let your head relax backward past the edge.
Support it with your hands if it feels heavy.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Use your hands to lift your head back up carefully.
Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Turn your head to one side as far as is comfortable.
Place one hand on your chin and the other on the back of your head.
Add light pressure to deepen the turn.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Sit or stand tall with your shoulders down.
Tilt your head back slightly.
Lower one ear toward the same shoulder.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Lie on a decline bench and hold the top edge above your head.
Bring your knees up and bend them.
Curl your hips off the bench, drawing your knees toward your chest.
Lower back down slowly without swinging.
Keep the movement controlled throughout.
Stand facing a wall with one foot back and your heel on the floor.
Keep your back leg straight and lean toward the wall.
Press your back heel down until you feel a stretch in the calf.
Keep your hips square and your toes pointing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
Extend one arm in front of you with the palm up.
Use your other hand to pull the fingers back toward you.
Keep your elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed.
Feel the stretch along the inner forearm.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch arms.
Set an incline bench and hold the bar at your upper chest.
Dip slightly through your legs to start momentum.
Drive the bar up while pressing with your arms.
Lock out above your chest, then lower under control.
Keep your core braced and your lower back from arching.
Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands by your sides.
Raise your legs to vertical.
Curl your hips up off the floor, pushing your feet toward the ceiling.
Lower your hips, then your legs, with control.
Keep your movement smooth and avoid swinging.
Lie on your back with your hands under your hips.
Bend your knees slightly and lift your feet off the floor.
Raise your legs until they are above your hips.
Lower slowly without letting your back arch.
Keep your core tight throughout.

exercises.exerciseName: leg raise hip lift with head up

instructions.originalText: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands by your sides.
Lift your head and shoulders slightly off the floor.
Raise your legs to vertical.
Push your hips a little off the floor, lifting your feet toward the ceiling.
Lower your hips and legs slowly with control.
Lie back on the machine and grip the handles.
Bend your knees and place your legs under the pads.
Curl your knees up toward your chest.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly until you feel tension, then repeat.
Adjust the seat and sit with your chest against the pad.
Hold the handles and set your feet firmly.
Curl your torso forward by contracting your abs.
Pause at the bottom.
Return slowly to the start without letting the weight drop.
Lie back on the decline seat and hook your feet under the pads.
Cross your arms or hold the handles.
Curl your torso up toward your knees.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower back slowly under control.
Attach a rope or bar to a high pulley and kneel facing away.
Hold it overhead with your elbows bent behind your head.
Keep your upper arms still and straighten your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at full extension.
Return slowly to the start.
Set the pad at hip level and hook your heels under the rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest and keep your body straight.
Bend forward at the hips with a flat back.
Lift your torso until it forms a straight line with your legs.
Do not overarch at the top, then lower with control.

exercises.exerciseName: cable curl with multipurpose v bar

instructions.originalText: Attach a multipurpose V bar to a low pulley and grip it with palms up.
Stand tall with your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly without letting your elbows drift.
Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Sit back with your feet flat and grip the handles.
Press upward until your arms are nearly straight.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back to the start.
Adjust the seat and grip the handles overhead.
Sit tall with your chest up.
Pull the handles down, driving your elbows toward your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
Return slowly to full stretch.
Set a decline bench to a steep angle and hook your feet under the pads.
Lie back and cross your arms over your chest.
Curl your torso up until you are sitting.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower slowly back down.

exercises.exerciseName: hammer grip pull up on dip cage

instructions.originalText: Grab the neutral grip handles with your palms facing each other.
Hang with your arms fully extended.
Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows down.
Pause with your chin above the bars.
Lower slowly to a full hang.

exercises.exerciseName: wide grip pull up on dip cage

instructions.originalText: Grab the wide handles with your palms facing forward.
Hang with your arms fully extended.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back.
Pause when your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
Sit on the machine with your back against the pad.
Place your legs against the pads, set wide.
Squeeze your legs together smoothly.
Pause for a moment when they meet.
Open slowly back to the start.
Set the bar in the rack and place it on your rear delts, below the traps.
Step back and set your feet shoulder width.
Lean forward slightly and sit your hips back and down.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive through your heels to stand, keeping your chest up.
Sit with your back against the pad and your legs inside the pads.
Hold the handles for stability.
Push your legs apart smoothly.
Pause at the widest point.
Return slowly without letting the weights crash.
Adjust the seat and grip the handles overhead.
Sit tall with your chest up.
Pull down until the handles reach chest level.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to full stretch.
Sit upright and grip the handles beside you.
Set your elbows tight to your sides.
Press down until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your triceps.
Return slowly to the start.
Adjust the seat so your upper arms rest on the pad.
Grip the handles with your palms up.
Curl up until your biceps are fully contracted.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
Sit with your back against the pad and your shins behind the roller.
Hold the handles.
Extend your knees until your legs are straight.
Squeeze your quads at the top.
Lower slowly under control.
Sit with your back against the pad and your shins behind the rollers.
Hold the handles.
Extend one leg until it is straight.
Lower it slowly.
Repeat with the other leg and keep alternating.
Step under the shoulder pads and set your feet shoulder width.
Release the safeties and stand tall.
Sit down and back until your thighs are parallel.
Drive through your heels to stand.
Keep your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.
Adjust the seat and place your arms against the pads.
Sit upright.
Raise your arms out to the sides until about shoulder height.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly to the start.
Stand tall with your feet wider than hip width.
Shift your weight onto one leg and bend that knee.
Keep the other leg straight, foot flat.
Push your hip out until you feel a stretch in the inner thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand tall, next to a wall if you need balance.
Cross one leg behind the other.
Lean your hips toward the side of your back leg.
Feel the stretch along the outer hip.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand facing a bench or step.
Place one heel on it with the knee slightly bent.
Keep your chest tall and hinge forward at the hips.
Feel the stretch in the hip and glute.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand next to a wall and lean on it with one hand.
Cross your outer leg behind the inner one.
Lean your hips toward the wall.
Keep both feet flat.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand tall near a support.
Pass one leg behind and under the other.
Push your hips gently to the side of the back leg.
Keep your torso upright.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bring one knee up and across your body.
Use the opposite hand to ease it toward the floor.
Keep your shoulders flat on the ground.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Lie on your back with your calves resting on a stability ball.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Roll the ball gently to bring your legs toward your chest.
Feel the stretch in the outer hip.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Lie on your back on a bench.
Cross one leg over your body and let it hang off the side.
Keep your shoulders flat.
Let gravity lower the leg slowly.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand facing a wall with one foot forward.
Place the ball of the forward foot against the wall, heel on the floor.
Lean your hips toward the wall.
Feel the stretch in the calf and Achilles.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand on a step with the ball of one foot on the edge.
Hold a rail for balance.
Lower your heel slowly below the step.
Keep the knee straight for the calf, then slightly bent for the soleus.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand facing a wall and step one foot back.
Keep the back leg straight and the heel down.
Bend your front knee and lean forward.
Feel the stretch in the back calf.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand near a wall or support.
Step one foot back with the heel down.
Slightly bend the back knee to target the lower Achilles.
Keep your back foot pointing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Sit on the floor with one leg straight.
Loop a towel around the ball of your foot or grip your toes.
Pull your toes toward your shin.
Keep your knee straight.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Crouch down with your hands on the floor for balance.
Extend one leg back with the heel down.
Press the heel toward the floor.
Keep your chest lifted.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Kneel on a mat with your toes tucked under.
Sit back onto your heels slowly.
Rest your hands on your thighs.
Ease off if the stretch is too sharp.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Release and shake out your feet.
Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward.
Lean forward, keeping your front heel on the floor.
Press your front knee over your toes.
Feel the stretch behind the ankle.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Sink into a deep squat with your heels down.
Hold on to a support if needed.
Gently shift your weight forward over your toes.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Stand up slowly.
Stand with your feet wide apart and toes pointing slightly out.
Bend your knees and place your hands on your thighs.
Shift your weight from side to side, sinking into the stretch.
Keep your chest tall and your back flat.
Hold for 20-30 seconds on each side.
Stand tall near a support.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Sit your hips back as if sitting into a chair.
Feel the stretch in the hip of the crossed leg.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.

exercises.exerciseName: standing raised leg hip adductor stretch

instructions.originalText: Stand tall and place one foot on a bench or raised surface to the side.
Keep your standing leg straight and your toes forward.
Shift your weight toward the raised leg side until you feel a stretch.
Keep your chest upright and your hips square.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
Stand next to a bench or low support.
Place one foot on it with the leg out to the side.
Keep your hips square.
Shift your weight toward the raised leg.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Kneel on all fours with your knees under your hips.
Extend one leg out to the side with the foot flat.
Sit your hips back toward the opposite heel.
Keep your back straight and your extended leg straight.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
Stand with your feet wide apart.
Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee.
Keep the other leg straight with the foot flat.
Keep your chest tall.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.

exercises.exerciseName: standing bent knee hip adductor stretch

instructions.originalText: Stand with your feet wide.
Bend one knee and lower into that side.
Keep your other leg straight.
Push the bent knee gently out with your hand.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Kneel on a mat, then lower your chest and forearms to the floor.
Slide your knees wide apart and sink your hips back toward your heels until you feel the inner thighs stretch.
Keep your breathing slow and stay relaxed, without bouncing.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
Sit on the floor with your legs spread wide.
Keep your knees pointing up.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine.
Walk your hands forward until you feel the stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Come up slowly.

exercises.exerciseName: hip abduction with flexion in front stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit on the floor with one leg bent in front of you.
Place the other leg to the side.
Lean your torso forward over the front shin.
Keep your hips grounded.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand with your feet wide apart, toes pointing slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee while the other leg stays straight, and feel the inner thigh stretch.
Keep your chest up and the straight leg's foot flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.exerciseName: lying leaning against the wall stretch

instructions.originalText: Lie on your back with your hips close to a wall.
Rest your legs straight up the wall.
Let your legs fall slowly out to the sides.
Relax and let gravity do the work.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Bring your legs together to finish.

exercises.exerciseName: abduction of one leg flexion stretch

instructions.originalText: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bend one knee, let it fall out to the side and, if needed, ease it down with your hand until the inner thigh stretches.
Keep your lower back and the opposite hip flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Have your partner lift one leg slightly and move it out to the side.
Keep your hips level.
Tell your partner to stop at a comfortable stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand with one heel on the floor in front of you.
Point your toes down.
Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back.
Keep the front leg nearly straight.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Switch sides and repeat.
Stand tall and step one foot forward, resting the heel on the floor with the toes pulled up.
Keep the front leg straight and the back knee slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a pull behind the thigh.
Keep your chest open and avoid rounding your spine.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Stand facing a low support and place one heel on it with the leg straight.
Hinge forward from the hips with a long back until you feel the back of the thigh stretch.
Keep your toes pointing up and your standing knee soft.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
Place one heel on a low bench or step in front of you with the leg straight.
Stand tall with the standing knee soft.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping your back flat, until you feel a stretch behind the raised thigh.
Keep your toes pointing up and breathe slowly.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.exerciseName: standing high leg bent knee hamstring stretch

instructions.originalText: Stand tall and place one heel on a high support with the knee slightly bent.
Lean your chest toward your thigh with a flat back until you feel the stretch behind the thigh.
Straighten the knee a little more as you get looser.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
Kneel on one knee and extend the other leg in front, heel on the floor and toes pulled up.
Place your hands on the floor or the front thigh for support.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a pull behind the extended leg.
Keep the extended knee straight but not locked.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.exerciseName: seated knee flexor and hip adductor stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit on the floor with your legs spread wide and knees straight.
Sit tall with your toes pointing up.
Hinge forward from the hips, walking your hands out in front of you.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the inner thighs and backs of the legs.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing slowly, then sit back up.
Sit on the floor with one leg straight out in front of you.
Reach toward your toes with a long back until you feel the back of the thigh stretch.
Keep your knee straight but not locked, and avoid rounding your back too much.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
Stand with your feet hip width apart.
Hinge at the hips and reach your hands down toward your shins or toes until you feel the back of the thighs stretch.
Let your head and neck hang relaxed and keep a slight bend in the knees.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.exerciseName: standing reach down hamstring crossed legs stretch

instructions.originalText: Stand tall and cross one foot over the other.
Hinge forward at the hips and reach toward the floor until the back of the thighs stretch.
Keep both legs fairly straight and let your head hang relaxed.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.exerciseName: seated hip external rotator and hip extensor stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit upright on the floor or a chair and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Gently press the raised knee down and lean your chest forward with a long back until the buttock stretches.
Keep your spine long instead of collapsing forward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.exerciseName: seated hip stretch with opposite leg from behind

instructions.originalText: Sit on the floor with one leg bent in front of you and the other leg bent behind.
Lean your chest forward over the front shin until you feel the stretch deep in the hip and buttock.
Keep both sit bones as level as you can.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.
Sit on a chair or the floor with one leg extended.
Point your toes away from you as far as is comfortable.
Gently press the top of the foot with your hand for a little extra stretch.
Keep the movement slow and avoid forcing the ankle.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Lie on your back with both legs straight.
Lift one leg toward the ceiling, holding behind the thigh or calf.
Keep the knee as straight as is comfortable and the other leg flat on the floor.
Gently draw the leg toward you until you feel a pull behind the thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.exerciseName: recumbent knee flexor stretch with towel

instructions.originalText: Lie on your back and loop a towel around the ball of one foot.
Raise that leg toward the ceiling, holding both ends of the towel.
Keep the knee nearly straight and the other leg flat on the floor.
Gently pull the towel until you feel a stretch behind the thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Lie on your back with your legs straight and relax completely.
Have a partner lift one leg by the heel, keeping the knee straight.
Tell your partner to stop when you feel a pull behind the thigh.
Keep your other leg and lower back flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs.
Stand facing a wall or step and place the ball of one foot against it with the heel on the floor.
Keep the leg straight.
Lean your hips gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the calf.
Keep your heel down and your back tall.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Stand on the edge of a step with the ball of one foot on it and hold a rail for balance.
Slowly lower that heel below the step until you feel the calf stretch.
Keep the knee straight to hit the calf, then bend it slightly to reach deeper into the soleus.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

exercises.exerciseName: plantar flexor and foot everter stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit with one leg extended and hold the foot with your hand.
Point the foot down and turn the sole slightly outward.
Gently press the foot until you feel a stretch along the front and outer ankle.
Move slowly and stop at a mild stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.exerciseName: plantar flexor and foot inverter stretch

instructions.originalText: Sit with one leg extended and hold the foot with your hand.
Point the foot down and turn the sole slightly inward.
Gently press the foot until you feel a stretch along the front and inner ankle.
Move slowly and stop at a mild stretch.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.exerciseName: tibial flexion stretch on wall bar

instructions.originalText: Stand facing the wall bars and place the front of one foot against a low bar.
